sentences.text: The prime allegation made against this petitioner is that the petitioner/A.4 was found in possession of tobacco, gutka and khainee and also in possession of ganja of 4 kgs.,
The products which are being transported will not come under the definition of food as per Section 3(j) of FSS Act.
Cigarettes, chewing tobacco, pan masala and chewing material with tobacco, are included in the tobacco products.
The tobacco products are only defined under COTPA Act and not under FSS Act.

3. The petitioner's main contention is that he is totally innocent of offence of possessing ganja and other banned products, police implicated him unnecessarily without any reasonable ground, he submits that possessing tobacco is not an offence.
As per COTPA Act the tobacco can be sold strictly following the rules under COTPA Act.
The quantity of ganja which is being allegedly transported in his vehicle is 4 kgs., and it is nota commercial quantity.
Hence, the petitioner approached this Court for granting anticipatory bail, apprehending his arrest by the police.
4. The nature and gravity of the accusation and the exact role of the accused must be properly comprehended before his arrest.

To attract the offences punishable under Sections offences punishable under Sections 270, 273, 328 read with 34 IPC, Section 20(b) read with 8(c) of NDPS Act, 1985 and Sections 59(i), 59(ii) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, er ee, To, there must be some material to show that those items are consisting of poisonous substances endangered to the life of human being, but no such allegation is found in the entire material including the mediator's report.
5.

Therefore, prima facie, I find no material against the petitioner/A.4 to establish the offences punishable under Sections offences punishable under Sections 270, 273, 328 read with 34 IPC,
Section 20(b) read with 8(c) of NDPS Act, 1985 and Sections S9i), SO(ii) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and that quantity of Ganja found in possession of petitioner is not a commercial quantity, consequently Section 37 of the NDPS Act has no application, apart from that,
tobacco products sale or possession is not an offence under FSS Act as held by this Court.

Therefore,
taking into consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner/A.4 can be enlarged on bail, as there is every apprehension of his arrest, in connection with the above crime.

6. In the result, Criminal Petition is allowed directing the Station House Officer, III Town Police Station, Visakhapatnam City, to release the petitioner/A.4 in connection with Cr.No.588/2020 on the file of III Town Police Station, Visakhapatnam City, for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 270, 273, 328 read with 34 IPC, Section 20(b) read with 8(c) of NDPS Act, 1985 and Sections 59(i), 59(ii) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, in the event of his arrest on executing a self-bond for Rs.20,000/- (Rupees twenty thousands only) with two sureties for a like sum each to the satisfaction of Station House Officer, III Town Police Station, Visakhapatnam City.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall also stand closed.
